subject: Pricing follow-up — target $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — target $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Volume / usage: you mentioned 200M tokens/month for month 1, with expected growth to ~1B tokens/month in Q1 2027 (peak bursts ~2B/month).
- Workload: mixed assistant + classification + some embeddings for semantic search; average prompt+response ~600 tokens.
- Budget: initial monthly commitment target $5k–$20k, but you're focused on unit economics and a target $/1M tokens to evaluate providers.
- Key decision criteria: unit price ($/1M tokens), latency (sub-200ms for short responses), predictable billing for forecasting, and data security/compliance.

Attached is a lightweight benchmark I pulled together (pricing-benchmark-20261006.xlsx) that compares typical public list pricing and modeled unit economics after batching/quantization for open models. High-level figures in the sheet; summary below. Can you confirm the volume and target $/1M you want us to model? Also, would you prefer a committed pilot (monthly commit + lower $/1M) or fully consumption-based?

Quick benchmark (modeled $/1M tokens) — rough, for discussion:
- OpenAI (pay-as-you-go): ~$20 / 1M tokens
- Anthropic (pay-as-you-go): ~$30 / 1M tokens
- Typical open-model hosts (managed): $12–25 / 1M tokens (depends on quantization and batching)
- Redwood (optimized pipeline + batching/quantization): modeled $6–12 / 1M tokens at scale / with reserved capacity assumptions

Suggested next steps:
1) Confirm target $/1M range you want modeled (e.g., $8–12 / 1M).
2) Share a small sample of traffic (anonymized prompts and token-length distribution) so we can run a quick cost projection.
3) If it looks promising, we propose a 3-month pilot with a modest commit (e.g., 500M tokens/month) and step-down pricing as volume ramps.

Thanks — I’ll slot a 30-min follow-up next week unless you’d rather jump on a call earlier.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: pricing-benchmark-20261006.xlsx (lightweight price model), redwood-cost-model-params.csv (assumptions)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Pat Lee <pat.lee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — target $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Thanks Vanessa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: confirmed ~200M tokens/month to start. We expect steady growth to ~800M–1B tokens/month by Jan–Feb, with short bursts approaching 2B in special campaigns.
- Target unit economics: our CFO is targeting ~$10 / 1M tokens as a wash vs our current budget for lower-priority workloads. If we can get <$10 / 1M for the open-model stack, we can justify shifting more production traffic off our current provider.
- Procurement preference: we prefer a committed pilot if the pricing is right (gives us predictability).

I'll pull together an anonymized sample of prompt/response lengths (should have that by Wednesday). Also: any elasticity on the first-month commit? We want to avoid a large upfront financial commitment.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex Morgan
Head of AI Platform, Acme Corp
alex.morgan@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T17:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — target $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Alex — perfect, thanks for the target. A few responses: 

- We can model pricing with a $10 / 1M tokens target and show what mix of reserved capacity + batching/quantization would be required. The attached sheet includes a scenario tab that shows a blended unit price at 200M, 500M, and 1B monthly volumes.
- Pilot structure we typically do: 90-day pilot with a modest minimum commit (e.g., 300–500M tokens/mo) + step-down pricing tiers as volume ramps. We can front-load credits for the first 30 days to reduce your initial cash outlay while still giving the predictability you want.
- Open questions for your sample data: average prompt tokens, average completion tokens, % of requests requiring low latency (<200ms), and % of embeddings vs completions. Those drive the cost delta.

Next steps: once we receive the sample traffic, Aditya (cc'd) can run a quick technical projection (latency & cost tradeoffs) and we can share a short SOW + pilot pricing sheet. When would be a good time for a 30-min technical call with Aditya and Marissa present?

Thanks — 
— Vanessa

P.S. Quick modeled snapshot from the sheet (blended unit price):
- 200M/mo (no reserve): ~$14 / 1M tokens
- 500M/mo (small reserve + quantization): ~$9 / 1M tokens
- 1B/mo (reserved capacity + aggressive batching): ~$6–7 / 1M tokens

Attachments: pricing-benchmark-20261006.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — target $/1M benchmarking vs OpenAI / Anthropic

Hi Alex — quick technical note as you prepare the sample traffic: 

1) Token distribution: please include percentiles (p50/p90/p99) for request sizes — cost and latency sensitivity vary a lot with long-tail completions.
2) Mix: embeddings are much cheaper per token when batched heavily; if >30% of your traffic is embeddings we can drive unit cost down substantially.
3) Model selection & quantization: using a 4-bit quantized open model + optimized kernels typically reduces inference cost 30–60% vs fp16 on the same hardware. We'll show modeled variance in the sheet.
4) Cold-cache vs warm-cache latency: if you have very bursty traffic, a warm KV cache reduces per-token cost for assistant flows.

I'll run two scenarios when you send the sample: (A) conservative (no reserve, pay-as-you-go host pricing) and (B) reserved + optimized stack. That will map to the $/1M numbers Vanessa included.

Happy to join the technical call — propose Thursday 10/08 at 10am PT?

— Aditya Rao
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
